seo.og_title: Safi Medina: Lanes, Souks & Daily Life
seo.og_description: Practical guide to walking Safi’s historic medina without rush.

name: Medina de Safi
hero_subtitle: Historic lanes, souks and everyday life by the Atlantic.

overview.title: The heart of old Safi
overview.p1: Safi’s medina is a compact historic quarter of whitewashed lanes, small squares and active souks. It remains a lived-in neighbourhood, not only a tourist set.
overview.p2: You will find crafts, food stalls and local shops. Orientation is easier than in larger imperial medinas; a couple of hours is enough for a first loop.
overview.p3: Combine it with the Sea Castle on the waterfront and, if you have time, the potters’ quarter on the hill.

moods.title: What to see in the medina
moods.subtitle: Lanes, markets and local rhythm.

1.title: Whitewashed alleys
1.desc: Wander without a fixed route; the medina is compact.

2.title: Local markets
2.desc: Spices, household goods and small craft stalls.

3.title: Lived-in quarter
3.desc: Morning and late afternoon feel most authentic.

food.title: Food in and near the medina
food.p1: Simple eateries and snack spots sit inside and at the edges of the old town.
food.li4: Keep valuables discreet in crowded lanes.
food.p2: Cash is the norm for small vendors.

1.title: Go early or late
1.desc: Morning and late afternoon are cooler and less crowded than midday.

2.title: Dress modestly
2.desc: As in any lived-in Moroccan medina, modest clothing is appreciated.

3.title: Link with the fortress
3.desc: From the medina you can walk down toward the Sea Castle and the port.

q1.question: How long for the medina?
q1.answer: One to two hours covers a comfortable first visit.

q2.question: Is it safe to walk alone?
q2.answer: Yes in daylight; stay aware of belongings in busy lanes.

q3.question: Are there fixed opening hours?
q3.answer: The medina is open; individual shops follow their own schedules.

q4.question: Can I take photos?
q4.answer: Yes of streets and buildings; ask before photographing people.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Optional. A guide helps with history; the layout is manageable alone.
